subject: Runtime telemetry & live-routing: service provider role demarcation
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@medbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: runtime telemetry/live-routing — are you a 'service provider' or 'operator'?

Jonas — thanks again for the demo last week. Two follow-ups from our security & privacy team as we prepare the pilot: one technical, one contractual.

1) Technical: in the draft dataflow we shared (attached), our traffic sometimes needs to be routed for latency-sensitive inference to the nearest region and, for a subset of requests, to a customer-dedicated pool. That routing emits short-lived telemetry (route id, latency bucket, model variant id) and we also snapshot small KV cache keys for debugging when an error occurs.

2) Contractual: under CCPA/CPRA the distinction between "service provider" and "operator" is material. We need to confirm whether Redwood, when doing this live routing and short-lived telemetry, is acting strictly as a service provider (limited-use, on behalf of controller) or has any capacity that would make you an operator. If you're a service provider, we also need the precise DPA language you will accept and any evidence (attestation, SOC report) that shows you treat routing telemetry as processing on our behalf.

Can you confirm:
- The operational model for routing and telemetry (who controls routing policy at runtime?)
- Whether the telemetry snapshots are retained beyond debugging windows and whether they're used for Redwood product analytics/optimization outside our account
- A short, plain-language statement we can circulate to legal describing your service-provider limitations for this use case

I've attached the draft-dataflow-diagram.png.

Elena Morris
Head of Product Operations
MedBridge Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@medbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: runtime telemetry/live-routing — are you a 'service provider' or 'operator'?

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the diagram. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Grace (Platform) to make sure we cover contract language and the runtime behavior. High level answers up front:

- Routing policy: the customer (MedBridge) configures routing policy via the API/console and may set rules for region, dedicated pools, and model variants. Redwood enforces those rules at runtime but does not unilaterally change them for other accounts. In that configuration, control stays with you.

- Telemetry: the short-lived telemetry you described (route id, latency bucket, model id) is emitted for request routing & debugging. By default we keep debug snapshots for 72 hours and they are scoped to the customer account; they are not used for cross-customer product analytics unless you opt in to anonymized performance telemetry sharing.

- Plain-language statement: see the attached redwood-sp-role-summary.pdf for an executive summary. Laura: can you convert that to suggested DPA/annex language (redline) we can insert into the addendum?

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to propose a redline for the DPA/service-provider clause specific to live routing & transient telemetry.
- Grace to confirm retention window and whether we can shorten it to 24 hours for pilot.
- Quick sync (30m) this week if that helps MedBridge legal.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@medbridge.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: runtime telemetry/live-routing — proposed DPA language

Elena, Jonas — thanks for the context. I reviewed the diagram and Redwood's runtime behavior. Below is a redline-style snippet we recommend for insertion into your addendum (we'll attach a .docx with tracked changes — see attached proposed-dpa-redline.docx).

--- suggested addendum text (plain text excerpt) ---
"For the purposes of applicable state privacy laws (including CCPA/CPRA), Redwood Inference ("Redwood") will act as a Service Provider/Processor with respect to MedBridge Health's Personal Information processed for the delivery of inference and routing services under the Agreement. Redwood's role is limited as follows:

1. Control & instruction: MedBridge controls routing policies and configuration. Redwood implements routing as instructed and does not access customer request payloads beyond what is required to perform routing and inference.

2. Telemetry & debugging snapshots: Redwood may collect transient telemetry (route_id, latency_bucket, model_variant_id) and ephemeral debugging snapshots (truncated KV keys, error trace) solely to perform, optimize, and debug the Services. Such telemetry and snapshots are retained for a maximum of 72 hours by default and are segregated by customer account. They will not be used for Redwood's product development, cross-customer benchmarking, or advertising unless MedBridge provides explicit, written consent to opt-in.

3. Limitations on secondary use: Redwood will not sell, license, or otherwise monetize MedBridge Personal Information. Any use of aggregated or pseudonymized telemetry for Redwood product improvement will be subject to prior de-identification and will not permit re-identification of MedBridge's end users.

4. Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood shall provide advance notice of subprocessors and will ensure subprocessors are bound by comparable contractual restrictions. For onshore fallback routing, Redwood will preferentially route to onshore dedicated pools where available and will provide written notice if cross-border routing is required for availability/latency reasons.

This language is intentionally conservative to align with the Service Provider/Processor boundary. Happy to tighten retention or add a carve-out for emergency incident investigations if you prefer."

--- end excerpt ---

Two practical notes: (a) we can shorten retention to 24 hours for the pilot if you need that in writing; (b) Grace, please confirm whether onshore-only fallback can be enforced by policy during the pilot and what the cost/throughput implications are.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Regulatory
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@medbridge.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: runtime telemetry/live-routing — proposed DPA language

Laura — thank you, that draft is exactly what we needed. Two quick follow-ups before we route to our procurement team:

- Can you confirm the 24-hour retention option in writing (we'd like that for the pilot). If 24h is supported, please state it as an explicit option in the addendum excerpt.
- For onshore fallback: can Redwood guarantee onshore-only routing if we pay for a dedicated reserved pool? If there's a hit to latency/cost we need an estimate for the procurement packet.

If you can send the small redline that includes 24h as an option and a note about dedicated-pool onshore fallback, we can circulate to procurement and SOC/privacy. If possible, include a pointer to the SOC2 attestation link or certificate number we can reference.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Elena Morris
Head of Product Operations
MedBridge Health
